findings.text: Public queuing interface that admits only sufficiently large non swapcache folios to a node and memory cgroup aware deferred split collection, recording partial mapping once with associated accounting.
Public removal interface for whole PMD sized reverse mappings, defined only when transparent huge page support is present and otherwise treated as unexpected.
Public resolution helpers that map a PMD address to its normal page or folio, yielding absence for mappings that lack a normal struct page.
Public reclamation attempt for a huge PMD range that reports whether the entry was handled, covering present and non present encodings with folio and deposited table cleanup.
Public split initiators that ensure alignment and huge or softleaf form before dividing a huge PMD, one usable with only the lock held and one managing notification bracketing.
Conditional lock acquisition helper that retains the PMD lock only while the entry remains huge and otherwise releases and reports absence.
Public munlock batching entry that pins the folio and either buffers it per CPU or flushes immediately when buffering is unavailable or unsuitable.
Reverse mapping removal distinguishes small and large folios and PTE versus PMD or PUD levels, with an alternate counting path when per page counts are disabled and rejection of other levels.
A large anonymous folio that becomes partly unmapped while still partly mapped and not already marked, excluding device private memory, is scheduled for deferred splitting to reclaim underuse.
Mapping count deltas update anonymous versus file mapped statistics, while PMD mapped deltas update distinct anonymous huge, shared memory, or file huge statistics with different accounting scopes.
Unlock handling is conservative: any folio touched in a locked virtual area is submitted for unlock, delegating correction of over broad unlocks to later reclaim.
Per CPU LRU caching suitability is limited to non large folios to avoid accounting imbalance from holding very large folios.

Teardown of a PMD span preserves correctness for partial huge coverage by splitting, prefers a fast huge path for full coverage, and otherwise descends to finer granularity with cooperative scheduling.
Normal page resolution filters special entries, file only and mixed mappings, shared zero pages, and out of range frame numbers, with branch behavior depending on architectural special bit support.
Whether a PMD carries a deposited page table follows architecture mandate, then huge zero versus device memory treatment, then anonymous ownership.

Huge PMD folio teardown removes reverse mapping only for present or device private cases, adjusts process counters by huge span, propagates dirtiness and recency from entry flags, and releases device private pins.
Folio lookup for a huge PMD uses the normal path when present and a softleaf path otherwise, with missing migration support treated as unexpected.
Diagnostic rendering of page table values supports common widths and reports overflow or unsupported widths textually rather than truncating.
Corrupt mapping diagnostics report process, level, entry encoding, page table chain, address, flags, ownership, indices, file operation hooks, plus stack and taint marking.
Deposited table teardown withdraws the table associated with a huge PMD, frees it, and updates the address space table count.
Deferred queuing protects memory cgroup lookup with a read side critical section and serializes list insertion with an IRQ saving per node list lock.
Huge PMD zap, conditional lock acquisition, and split paths all serialize against concurrent table changes with the PMD lock, held across validation and mutation.
Full PMD split brackets the locked mutation with invalidation notifications covering the whole huge span.
Munlock batching serializes per CPU buffer access with a local lock.
Diagnostic page table dump relies on locking established by its caller and is not safe as an independent lockless walk.
Unmap accounting moves between fully mapped, partly mapped, and fully unmapped states using atomic adjustments with tolerance for concurrent adds that may race ahead.

Deferred split membership progresses from eligibility screening to at most once marking of partial state and then insertion, with a global toggle gating fully mapped insertions and a warning against regression of partial state.
Range zapping advances cooperatively across PMD units, retrying the same unit when finer teardown reports incomplete progress.
Bad mapping alerts allow an initial burst then enforce a quiet interval, counting suppressed reports for later summary.

Huge PMD splitting aborts early for special huge areas and shared zero pages, and treats file, migration, and device private encodings with distinct teardown that avoids generic page table construction.
Range teardown entry coordinates huge fast paths and fine grained descent to remove mappings over an address interval.
Normal page resolution serves as the shared gate deciding whether a PMD frame number corresponds to accountable memory.
Concurrent mapping additions can race removals, requiring clamping of negative results and acceptance of zero progress rather than corrupting counts.

Complete unmap deliberately leaves anonymous association in place because a racing addition could otherwise observe a cleared state inconsistently; final reset is deferred to the page freeing path where mapping is known stable.
Frame numbers beyond the highest directly mapped frame are treated as table corruption and trigger bounded diagnostics rather than conversion to a struct page.
Very small compound orders are silently excluded from deferred queuing because they lack space for linkage, trading minor retained memory for simplicity.
Device private folios neither join deferred splitting nor follow normal reclamation, remaining pinned and requiring explicit reference release.
Encountering a non present huge entry without migration support indicates an unexpected configuration and raises a one time warning.
Huge PMD span, page count, and mask constants define full coverage granularity, accounting width, and alignment for zap, split, and counter updates.
A threshold constant distinguishes whole folio mapping counts from partial counts during unmap accounting.
Virtual area flags distinguish locked areas needing unlock handling from file only and mixed mappings needing special normal page treatment.
Page table level selectors distinguish PTE, PMD, and PUD handling for reverse mapping removal and special bit support.
